title: Franklin's Arrival in Philadelphia with Three Rolls of Bread

source_brief: This is a passage from Benjamin Franklin's own autobiography (Project Gutenberg ebook #148). After a difficult overnight boat journey, the young Franklin -- about 17, penniless, tired, and dressed in his work clothes -- walks into Philadelphia for the first time. Hungry, he asks a baker for bread and, not knowing the local prices or bread types, ends up buying three large puffy rolls for threepence. Carrying one roll under each arm and eating the third, he walks up Market Street past the house of his future father-in-law, whose daughter sees him from the doorway and privately thinks he looks awkward and ridiculous. Once full, he gives his two remaining rolls to a woman and child who had shared his overnight boat trip. He then follows a crowd into a Quaker meeting house, where, exhausted from travel, he falls asleep until the meeting ends and someone kindly wakes him.
